The students in a particular school are split among three classes, class $1$, class $2$, and class $3$.

- Class $1$ contains $25%$ of the students in the school, and $55%$ of those students take biology.
- Class $2$ contains $35%$ of the students in the school, and $40%$ of those students take biology.
- Class $3$ contains $40%$ of the students in the school.

If $45%$ of students in the entire school are female, $80%$ of female students take biology, and $70%$ of biology students are female, what is the probability that a randomly selected student from class $3$ takes biology? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Arthur and Sara are finding the best recipe for chocolate muffins, and they test three different oven cooking modes, mode $1$, mode $2$, and mode $3$. They also try two types of yeast, A and B.

- They use mode $1$ to cook the $45%$ of their muffins, and $80%$ of those muffins turn out well.
- They use mode $2$ to cook the $35%$ of their muffins.
- They use mode $3$ to cook the $20%$ of their muffins, and $90%$ of those muffins turn out well.

If $65%$ of all muffins were prepared with yeast A, $82%$ of yeast A muffins turn out well, and $68%$ of good muffins were prepared with yeast A, what is the probability that a randomly chosen muffin cooked with mode $2$ turned out well? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A local newspaper is sold by three distributors, $1,$ $2,$ and $3.$

- Distributor $1$ gets $36%$ of the copies.

- Distributor $2$ gets $23%$ of the copies, and $92%$ of those copies are sold.

- Distributor $3$ gets $41%$ of the copies, and $95%$ of those copies are sold.

If $3%$ of all copies have some printing defect, $70%$ of defective copies are sold, and $2.5%$ of sold copies are defective, what is the probability that a randomly chosen copy bought by distributor $1$ is sold? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

:knowledge-point/title: Solving for an Unknown Conditional Probability
